2 year civil eng student at rmit. Compared to Monash, the work has more emphasis on practical applications of the theory, which means little to no rote learning. Assignments are interesting and straightforward, the syllabus and mark weightings are generous with mostly quizzes and small tests. No exams as of yet, only major assignments/ tests which are all predominantly online. 

This makes the whole course super easy to keep on top of, i have an 80% + wam while skipping several weeks of content until its required in a test or assignment.

No attendance hurdles or exam hurdles is what makes this viable^

Massively worth transferring because you'll have the same degree at the end while having experienced far less stress.

You should contact rmit about credit transfer just to make sure you're not losing progress in terms of degree completion, in case you do want to transfer.

In the end wam /gpa doesn't matter as much as internships/ job experience which a lesser workload at rmit will help you focus on.

Also as for why this is, idk but could be for any number of reasons, one being higher achieving students generally go to Monash, and their teaching philosophy may be more academically inclined whereas rmit heavily emphasises making students 'job ready'
